rules.title: Gross rental rate increase cap
rules.requirement: An owner of residential real property shall not, over any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, based on the lowest gross rental rate charged during the prior 12 months, excluding any owner-offered discounts, incentives, concessions, or credits accepted by the tenant.
rules.key_value: 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower
rules.exemptions: Housing restricted by deed, regulatory restriction, or agreement as affordable housing, or subject to subsidies for very low, low, or moderate income families. [CIV § 1947.12(d)(1)]; Dormitories owned and operated by an institution of higher education or a K-12 school. [CIV § 1947.12(d)(2)]; Housing subject to local rent or price control consistent with Costa-Hawkins that restricts annual rental rate increases to an amount less than that provided in subdivision (a). [CIV § 1947.12(d)(3)]; Housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, unless the housing is a mobilehome. [CIV § 1947.12(d)(4)]; Separately alienable residential real property (including mobilehomes) provided the owner is not a REIT, corporation, LLC with a corporate member, or mobilehome park management, and tenants were provided the required written statutory notice. [CIV § 1947.12(d)(5)]; Two-unit properties within a single structure where the owner occupied one unit as principal residence at the start of tenancy and continues in occupancy, and neither unit is an ADU or JADU. [CIV § 1947.12(d)(6)]; A homeowner of a mobilehome, as defined in Section 798.9. [CIV § 1947.12(j)]
rules.interaction: This section is not intended to expand or limit the authority of local governments to establish local policies regulating rents consistent with Chapter 2.7 (commencing with Section 1954.50), nor does it affect existing authority of a local government to adopt or maintain rent controls or price controls consistent with that chapter.
rules.quoted_span: Subject to subdivision (b), an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase. An owner who demands, accepts, receives, or retains any payment of rent in excess of the maximum rent allowed by this section shall be liable in a civil action to the tenant from whom those payments are demanded, accepted, received, or retained for all of the following:

(A) The owner is not any of the following:
